AGENDA
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  JUNE 7, 2022
UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE, MEETINGS WILL BE CONDUCTED PURSUANT TO THE PROVISIONS OF
ASSEMBLY BILL 361, WHICH ALLOWS COUNCIL MEMBERS TO PARTICIPATE FROM A REMOTE
LOCATION WITHOUT LISTING A PHYSICAL LOCATION. TO PROVIDE COMMENTS DURING A MEETING:
YOU MAY ATTEND THE MEETING, SEND AN EMAIL TO: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, OR JOIN THE
ZOOM MEETING BY CALLING: (669) 900-6833 OR USING THE ZOOM APP WITH THE FOLLOWING LINK:
https://us02web.zoom.us/j/7095732685; MEETING ID: 709 573 2685. THE MEETING MAY BE VIEWED
THROUGH ZOOM, FIOS CHANNEL 32 OR CHARTER CHANNEL 3, OR ON THE CITY'S WEBPAGE AT:
https://www.norwalk.org/city-hall/meeting-agendas-393.
  6:15 PM
  NORWALK CITY HALL/COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  AND VIA VIDEOCONFERENCE

  Rick Ramirez, Mayor
  Ana Valencia, Vice Mayor
  Tony Ayala, Councilmember
  Jennifer Perez, Councilmember
  Margarita L. Rios, Councilmember
  Public Comment: Comments may be made in person, submitted via email at: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, or through
  the video conference during the designated time on any item on the agenda or on any other matter within the jurisdiction
  subject to the rules of decorum described in Norwalk Municipal Code §2.08.020. The maximum time allowed is three
  minutes.

  Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless
  certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain
  matters for consideration at a future City Council meeting.

  Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the Council:

  • Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
  • Comments should be directed to the City Council as a whole and not directed to individual Councilmembers.

  Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City
  meeting or other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk's Department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening
  devices are available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and
  documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability.
  Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring
  that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

  Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it
  has been posted will also be made available for public inspection.

  Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City Clerk's Department, City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard
  during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday - Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every other Friday;
  telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

  STUDY SESSION MEETING – 5:00 p.m.
 CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Ramirez

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FOR CLOSED SESSION MATTERS

CLOSED SESSION

  I.  PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE §54957.6; CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATOR.
  Negotiating on behalf of the City: Jesus M. Gomez, City Manager regarding negotiations with the
  Norwalk City Employees Association.

  II.  PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE §54957.6; CONFERENCE WITH LABOR NEGOTIATOR.
  Negotiating on behalf of the City: Jesus M. Gomez, City Manager regarding negotiations with the
  Norwalk Association of Management Employees.

RECESS

  REGULAR MEETING – 6:00 p.m.

CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Ramirez

INVOCATION
  April Reutter
  Pray Norwalk

FLAG SALUTE
  Juliet Reed
  5th Grade Norwalk student

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION REPORT

CITY COUNCIL COMMENTS

  a.  Report of City Council Travel

SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS - None

CITY MANAGER COMMENTS

  1.  COVID-19 Update.

  2.  Memorial Day Ceremony video.

  3.  Preventing Vehicle Theft video.

  4.  Bi-Weekly Review.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Consent calendar items are considered routine matters which may be enacted by one motion and roll call vote.
Any item may be removed from the consent calendar and considered separately by City Council.
 1.  MEETING MINUTES – Staff recommends City Council approve the minutes of the meetings of May 16
  and 17, 2022. 825-04

  Minutes

2.  PAYROLL – Staff recommends City Council approve the payroll for the periods May 1, 2022 – May 14,
  2022 totaling $960,862.35 and May 15, 2022 – May 28, 2022 totaling $983,856.85. 630

  Report

3.  COMMERCIAL DEMANDS – Staff recommends City Council approve the warrant register period May
  10, 2022 through May 23, 2022 in the total amount of $3,657,049.68. 640

  Warrant Register

4.  CLAIMS AGAINST THE CITY – Staff recommends City Council deny the claims filed by Lydia Coppola
  and Herman Flores. 830-03/06

  Report

5.  GENERAL MUNICIPAL ELECTION – NOVEMBER 8, 2022 – RESOLUTION NOS. 22-25 - CALLING
  ELECTION AND 22-26 - CONSOLIDATION WITH LOS ANGELES COUNTY REGISTRAR-
  RECORDER - Staff recommends City Council adopt:

  a.  Resolution No. 22-25, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK
  CALLING FOR THE HOLDING OF A GENERAL MUNICIPAL ELECTION TO BE HELD ON
  NOVEMBER 8, 2022, FOR THE ELECTION OF CERTAIN OFFICERS AS REQUIRED BY THE
  PROVISIONS OF THE LAWS OF THE STATE OF CALIFORNIA RELATING TO GENERAL LAW
  CITIES; and

  b.  Resolution No. 22-26, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK
  REQUESTING THE BOARD OF SUPERVISORS OF THE COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES TO
  CONSOLIDATE THE CITY OF NORWALK’S GENERAL MUNICIPAL ELECTION TO BE HELD ON
  TUESDAY, NOVEMBER 8, 2022 WITH THE STATEWIDE GENERAL ELECTION TO BE HELD
  ON THE DATE PURSUANT TO §10403 OF THE ELECTIONS CODE. 845-03

  Report

6.  RESOLUTION NO. 22-27 – AUTHORIZATION TO APPLY FOR A WATER REPLENISHMENT
  DISTRICT SAFE DRINKING WATER PROGRAM GRANT TO IMPLEMENT WELLHEAD TREATMENT
  FOR WELL NO. 10 - Staff recommends City Council adopt Resolution No. 22-27, A RESOLUTION OF
  THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF NORWALK AUTHORIZING DATA TO BE PREPARED AND AN
  APPLICATION TO BE SIGNED AND FILED WITH THE WATER REPLENISHMENT DISTRICT OF
  SOUTHERN CALIFORNIA TO OBTAIN GRANT FUNDING THROUGH THE SAFE DRINKING WATER
  PROGRAM TO IMPLEMENT WELLHEAD TREATMENT FOR WELL NO. 10. 1070-11

  Report

7.  PROJECT NO. 7442 – WATER MAIN REPLACEMENT ON PIONEER BOULEVARD FROM 160TH TO
  166TH STREET - AWARD OF CONTRACTS FOR CONSTRUCTION IMPROVEMENTS AND
  PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT FOR CONSTRUCTION SUPPORT SERVICES – Staff
  recommends City Council:

  a.  award a contract to Stephen Doreck Equipment Rentals, in the amount of $2,747,515 for City
  Project No. 7442, Water Main Replacement on Pioneer Boulevard from 160th to 166th Street; and
  authorize the City Manager to execute the agreement and any amendments, provided there is
  funding in the budget, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney; and

  b.  award a contract to Z&K Consultants, in the amount of $287,284 for Construction Management,
  Inspection, and Testing Services for the project; and authorize the City Manager to execute the
  agreement and any amendments, provided there is funding in the budget, on behalf of the City, in
  a form approved by the City Attorney. 1005-04-7442

  Report
   8.  AMENDMENT NO. 2 - FEDERAL ADVOCACY SERVICES - Staff recommends City Council approve
  Amendment No. 2 with Carpi & Clay from July 1, 2022 through June 30, 2024 at a cost of $24,000
  annually; and authorize the City Manager to execute the agreement, and any amendments provided
  there is funding in the budget, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney. 120-01

  Report

  9.  ACCESS  CONTROL  ELECTRONIC  CARD  READER  SYSTEM  INSTALLATION  –
  TRANSPORTATION/PUBLIC SERVICES FACILITY - Staff recommends City Council approve the
  purchase and installation of an access control electronic card reader system for the
  Transportation/Public with ASSI Security Inc., in the amount of $65,187.61; and authorize the City
  Manager to execute the proposal and any amendments on behalf of the City, provided there is funding
  in the budget, in a form approved by the City Attorney. 810-01/920-10

  Report

  10. LAND MOBILE RADIO SYSTEM CAPITAL LEASE AGREEMENT - Staff recommends City Council
  approve a two (2) year agreement with Mobile Relay Associates, LLC in an amount not to exceed
  $131,976 from July 1, 2022 through June 30, 2024, with three (3) additional one (1) year option for the
  period of July 1st through June 30th of each year thereafter, for a Digital Land Mobile Radio (LMR), for
  a total contract value of $263,952 subject to City Council’s approval of the budget; and authorize the
  City Manager to execute the agreement and any amendments provided there is funding in the budget,
  on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney. 110-04/810-13

  Report

  11. AGREEMENT AMENDMENT NO. 9 – PARKING MANAGEMENT SERVICES – ADJUSTING AMOUNT
  AND EXTENDING TERM TO JUNE 30, 2023 – Staff recommends City Council approve Amendment
  No. 9, extending the term of the agreement with Parking Concepts, Incorporated, for an additional one-
  year term beginning July 5, 2022; and authorize the City Manager to execute the amendment on behalf
  of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney. 810-16/920-04

  Report

  12. AGREEMENT AMENDMENT - CITY TRAFFIC ENGINEERING SERVICE FOR TRAFFIC
  ENGINEERING SERVICES - Staff recommends City Council approve agreement amendment for
  traffic-engineering services with Willdan Engineering for FY 2022/23, increasing the existing contract
  amount to $130,000 and extending the term through June 30, 2023; and authorize the City Manager to
  execute the amendment and any further amendments provided there is funding in the budget, on
  behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney. 1050/810-23

  Report

  13. AGREEMENT AMENDMENT NO. 8 - CONSULTING SERVICES FOR OIL PAYMENT PROGRAM
  COMMUNITY OUTREACH AND PUBLIC EDUCATION SERVICES - Staff recommends City Council
  approve Amendment No. 8 with KJ Services Environmental Consulting in the amount of $16,000
  annually from July 1, 2022 through June 30, 2023 for consultant services associated with the Oil
  Payment and Beverage Container Grant Program; and authorize the City Manager to execute the
  amendment on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney. 1065-04-01

  Report

  14. 2022 APPLICATIONS FOR RETAIL FIREWORKS SALES PERMITS - Staff recommends City Council
  approve the organizations eligible to obtain retail fireworks permits and authorize issuance of permits.
  612-08

  Report

APPOINTMENTS

  15. ADVISORY BODIES – Staff recommends City Council make appointments to fill the vacancies on the
  various City advisory bodies. 200

  Report
 PUBLIC HEARINGS

  16. RESOLUTION NO. 22-28 - SETTING SEWER SERVICE CHARGE FOR FISCAL YEAR 2022/23 AND
  ORDERING THAT SUCH CHARGE BE COLLECTED ON THE TAX ROLL - Staff recommends City
  Council consider adopting Resolution No. 22-28, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE
  CITY OF NORWALK APPROVING THE ANNUAL SEWER REPORT AND LEVYING AN ANNUAL
  SEWER SERVICE CHARGE FOR FISCAL YEAR 2022/23 PURSUANT TO CHAPTER 13.14 OF THE
  NORWALK MUNICIPAL CODE AND ORDERING THE ANNUAL SEWER SERVICE CHARGE TO BE
  COLLECTED ON THE COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES TAX ROLL. 637

  Report

  17. RESOLUTION NO. 22-29 - FISCAL YEAR 2022/23 ANNUAL ACTION PLAN FOR THE COMMUNITY
  DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT AND HOME – Staff recommends City Council:

  a.  adopt Resolution No. 22-29, A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK APPROVING THE COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT BLOCK GRANT AND HOME
  INVESTMENT PARTNERSHIPS PROGRAM FISCAL YEAR 2022/23 ANNUAL ACTION PLAN, AN
  APPLICATION FOR FUNDING, AND AUTHORIZING THE CITY MANAGER TO EXECUTE AND
  TRANSMIT ALL REQUIRED DOCUMENTS TO THE UNITED STATES DEPARTMENT OF
  HOUSING AND URBAN DEVELOPMENT;

  b.  authorize the City Manager to execute agreements and any amendments with social service
  agencies for the provision of services funded under the Annual Action Plan, on behalf of the City, in
  forms approved by the City Attorney; and

  c.  authorize the Director of Community Development to execute a Memorandum of Understanding
  with City Departments and homeless referral organizations for the provision of services funded
  under the Annual Action Plan. 315

  Report

REPORT

  18. FISCAL YEAR 2022/23 PROPOSED BUDGET - The Fiscal Year 2022/23 Proposed Budget is
  presented for discussion and direction. 610

  Report

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

ADJOURNMENT

I hereby certify under penalty of perjury under the laws of the State of California that the foregoing agenda was posted
on the City Hall bulletin board not less than 72 hours prior to the meeting. Dated June 3, 2022.

Theresa Devoy, CMC
City Clerk
